'''''Asphodelus fistulosus''''' is a species of plant known as '''hollow-stemmed asphodel''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17}}</ref> '''onionweed''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=ASFI2|taxon=Asphodelus fistulosus|accessdate=8 January 2016}}</ref> '''onion-leafed asphodel''', and '''pink asphodel'''. It is native to the [[Mediterranean]] region as well as the [[Arabian Peninsula]], [[Transcaucasus]], and [[Madeira]].<ref name = powo>{{cite web |title=''Asphodelus fistulosus'' L. |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:531496-1 |website=[[Plants of the World Online]] |publisher=[[Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew]] |access-date=17 February 2025}}</ref>

It is an [[noxious weed|invasive exotic weed]] in the United States, with significant infestations in [[California]], [[Arizona]], [[New Mexico]], and [[Texas]]. It is listed as a [[Federal Noxious Weed Act of 1974|Federal Noxious Weed]] by the [[United States Department of Agriculture]]. It is also a common weed in parts of Australia, New Zealand, and Mexico, and it thrives in any area with a [[Mediterranean climate]].

It is an annual or short-lived perennial herb growing a hollow stem up to {{cvt|70|cm|0}} tall. The root system has a series of [[tuber]]-like parts at the base of the stem. The plant takes the form of a large tuft of onion-like rounded hollow leaves up to {{cvt|30|cm|0}} long. The [[inflorescence]] is a [[panicle]] with widely spaced flowers. Each flower is {{cvt|5–12|mm|in|1}} wide with six [[tepal]]s which are generally white or very pale pink with a neat central longitudinal stripe of brown to reddish-purple. The flowers are diurnal, closing at night and in overcast or low-light weather conditions. The fruit is a rounded capsule containing six seeds.

Two subspecies are accepted.<ref name = powo/>
*''Asphodelus fistulosus'' subsp. ''fistulosus'' – Mediterranean basin, Arabian Peninsula, and Transcaucasus
*''Asphodelus fistulosus'' subsp. ''madeirensis'' {{small|Simon}} – Madeira
